info.title: IPGeolocation.io: Astronomy API
info.description:
Retrieve astronomical information including rise and set times for the
Sun and Moon, current position, distance from Earth, and azimuth for
a specific location and date.

The Astronomy API provides accurate-enough results (within approximately
one minute) suitable for applications like sunrise/sunset timers, though
not intended for precision astronomical purposes.

Astronomical information can be retrieved using multiple lookup inputs:

- Location address (preferably city-level)
- Geographic coordinates (latitude and longitude)
- IPv4 or IPv6 address

If no lookup parameter is provided, the API resolves the location using
the public IP address of the requesting client.

Two endpoints are available:

- **Single-date lookup** (`GET /v3/astronomy`) returns astronomical
  information for a specific location and date, including sunrise,
  sunset, moonrise, moonset, twilight phases, golden hour, blue hour,
  sun and moon position data, and moon phase.

- **Time series lookup** (`GET /v3/astronomy/timeSeries`) returns
  astronomical information across a date range (up to 90 days) for a
  specific location.

## Authentication

Two authentication methods are supported:

### API Key

Pass your API key as the `apiKey` query parameter on every request. You can find your
key in the [IPGeolocation dashboard](https://app.ipgeolocation.io/). Store it in
server-side environment variables. Avoid exposing it in client-side JavaScript.

### Request Origin (CORS)

Available on paid plans only. Whitelist your domain in the dashboard under the
"API Keys" section. Once configured, requests from that domain (and all its subdomains)
are accepted without passing `apiKey`. Enter your root domain (e.g. `example.com`),
not the full URL.

Each plan has a limit on the number of extra API keys and request origins:

| Plan | Extra API Keys + Request Origins |
|---|---|
| Free | 0 |
| Starter | 1 |
| Plus | 2 |
| Pro | 2 |
| Business | 3 |
| Premium | 3 |

Plans are sized by API credits, not requests: Free includes 1,000 credits
per day; Starter 150,000 credits/month; Plus 500,000; Pro 1,000,000;
Business 2,000,000; Premium 5,000,000.

Additional keys or origins can be added for $2.50 per month each.

## Credit Usage

Credits are charged only for successful **HTTP 200** responses. The
exact number of credits consumed by a request is returned in the
`X-Credits-Charged` response header.

- Each successful **Astronomy lookup** consumes **1 credit** per request.

## Lookup Parameter Priority

If multiple lookup parameters are provided in a request, the API resolves
the location using the following priority order:

1. Geographic coordinates (`lat` and `long`)
2. `location`
3. `ip`

The `ip` parameter is always validated, even when a higher-priority parameter is
present. An invalid `ip` returns HTTP 400, and a bogon or private `ip` returns
HTTP 423.

If none of the lookup parameters are provided, the API resolves the
location using the public IP address of the requesting client.

## Time Zone Behavior

By default, all astronomical event timestamps (sunrise, sunset, moonrise,
moonset, twilight phases, solar noon, etc.) are returned in the local
time of the resolved geographic location.

If the optional `time_zone` parameter is provided, all timestamps are
converted to the specified IANA timezone. In this case, timestamps are
returned as full date-time values (`yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`) rather than
time-only values (`HH:mm`), and a `time_zone` field is included in
the `astronomy` response object.

Due to timezone differences, some events may appear on a different
calendar date after conversion.

tags.name: Astronomy
tags.description:
API endpoints for retrieving astronomical information for a given
location, including sunrise and sunset times, moonrise and moonset
times, twilight phases, golden hour and blue hour windows, solar noon,
sun and moon position data (altitude, azimuth, distance), and moon
phase.

A time series endpoint is also available to retrieve daily astronomical
data across a date range of up to 90 days.

get.description:
Returns astronomical information for a specific location and date,
including:

- Sunrise and sunset times
- Moonrise and moonset times
- Morning and evening twilight phases (astronomical, nautical, civil)
- Golden hour and blue hour windows (morning and evening)
- Solar noon, day length, and astronomical midnight
- Sun position: altitude, azimuth, distance from Earth
- Moon position: altitude, azimuth, distance from Earth, parallactic angle
- Moon phase, illumination percentage, and moon phase angle (`moon_angle`)

The location can be resolved using geographic coordinates (`lat` and
`long`), a location address (`location`), or an IP address (`ip`).

If multiple lookup parameters are provided, the API resolves the
location using the following priority order:

1. `lat` and `long`
2. `location`
3. `ip`

The `ip` parameter is always validated, even when a higher-priority parameter is
present. An invalid `ip` returns HTTP 400, and a bogon or private `ip` returns
HTTP 423.

If none of the lookup parameters are provided, the API resolves the
location using the public IP address of the requesting client.

By default, results are calculated for the current date. Pass the
`date` parameter to retrieve data for a specific date.

Each successful lookup consumes **1 credit**.

X-Credits-Charged.description: Number of API credits consumed by this request.

400.description:
Bad Request – Possible reasons include:
  - If the provided IPv4 or IPv6 address is invalid.
  - If special character(s) `[ ] { } | ^ \`` is passed in the
    API URL either as a parameter or its value, especially in the
    case of an API key.
  - If the provided `date` is not in the format `yyyy-MM-dd`.
  - If an invalid or unsupported `lang` parameter is provided.
  - If only one of `lat` or `long` is provided; both must be
    provided together.
  - If the provided values for `lat` and `long` are not numbers,
    or fall outside the acceptable ranges. Valid latitude range is
    **-90 to 90**; valid longitude range is **-180 to 180**.
    Non-numeric values, and values written with an exponent larger
    than 50 (for example `1e51`), return
    `Invalid value '1e51' for parameter 'lat'.` A non-numeric
    `elevation` returns the same message for `elevation`.
  - If the provided `elevation` value exceeds the maximum allowed
    value of **10,000 meters**.
  - If the provided `time_zone` is invalid or unrecognized.
  - If the provided IPv4 or IPv6 address does not exist in our
    database.

get.description:
Returns daily astronomical information for a specific location across
a date range.

The response contains an array of daily astronomy records, each
including sunrise, sunset, moonrise, moonset, twilight phases,
solar noon, day length, and moon phase. Real-time positional data
(altitude, azimuth, distance) is not included in time series
responses.

The location can be resolved using geographic coordinates (`lat` and
`long`), a location address (`location`), or an IP address (`ip`).

**Date range constraints:**
- Both `dateStart` and `dateEnd` are required.
- The range can cover at most **90 days**, counting both `dateStart` and
  `dateEnd` (so `dateEnd` can be at most 89 days after `dateStart`).
  `dateEnd` must not be before `dateStart`.
- Both past and future dates are supported within the 90-day window.

Each successful lookup consumes **1 credit** per request.

X-Credits-Charged.description: Number of API credits consumed by this request.

400.description:
Bad Request – Possible reasons include:
  - If the provided IPv4 or IPv6 address is invalid.
  - If special character(s) `[ ] { } | ^ \`` is passed in the
    API URL either as a parameter or its value.
  - If `dateStart` or `dateEnd` is not in the format `yyyy-MM-dd`
    (`` `dateStart` must be in 'yyyy-MM-dd' format `` or
    `` `dateEnd` must be in 'yyyy-MM-dd' format ``).
  - If the range covers more than **90 days**, counting both
    `dateStart` and `dateEnd` (`Date range cannot exceed 90 days.`).
  - If `dateEnd` is before `dateStart`
    (`End date must be on or after start date.`).
  - If `dateStart` or `dateEnd` is missing
    (`Required request parameter 'dateStart' is missing`) or empty.
  - If only one of `lat` or `long` is provided; both must be
    provided together.
  - If the provided values for `lat` and `long` are not numbers,
    or fall outside the acceptable ranges. Non-numeric values, and
    values written with an exponent larger than 50 (for example
    `1e51`), return `Invalid value '1e51' for parameter 'lat'.` A
    non-numeric `elevation` returns the same message for
    `elevation`.
  - If the provided `elevation` value exceeds **10,000 meters**.
  - If the provided `time_zone` is invalid or unrecognized.
  - If the provided IPv4 or IPv6 address does not exist in our
    database.

Lat.name: lat
Lat.description:
Latitude coordinate of the location. Must be provided together with
the `long` parameter.

Valid latitude values range from **-90 to 90**.

Omit this parameter when it is not needed. When using coordinates,
provide both latitude and longitude.

Long.name: long
Long.description:
Longitude coordinate of the location. Must be provided together with
the `lat` parameter.

Valid longitude values range from **-180 to 180**.

Omit this parameter when it is not needed. When using coordinates,
provide both latitude and longitude.

Location.name: location
Location.description:
Address or location name used to determine the astronomical
information. Typically a city-level or region-level address such as
`New York, USA` or `London, UK`.

When this parameter is used, the API returns a `location` object
containing geolocation details alongside the `astronomy` object.

Ip.name: ip
Ip.description:
An IPv4 or IPv6 address used to resolve the location for the
astronomical lookup. When omitted, the API resolves the public IP
of the requesting client.

When the lookup is performed using an IP address, the response
includes additional geolocation fields in the `location` object
such as continent, country codes, district, and zipcode.

Date.name: date
Date.description:
Date for which to retrieve astronomical information.

Must be in `yyyy-MM-dd` format. Defaults to the current date if
not provided (taken in `time_zone` when that parameter is given). All
astronomical information is calculated at the current time of day at the
resolved location, or in `time_zone` when that parameter is given.

DateStart.name: dateStart
DateStart.description:
Start date of the time series range.

Must be in `yyyy-MM-dd` format. The range can cover at most **90 days**,
counting both `dateStart` and `dateEnd` (so `dateEnd` can be at most 89 days
after `dateStart`). `dateEnd` must not be before `dateStart`.

DateEnd.name: dateEnd
DateEnd.description:
End date of the time series range.

Must be in `yyyy-MM-dd` format. The range can cover at most **90 days**,
counting both `dateStart` and `dateEnd` (so `dateEnd` can be at most 89 days
after `dateStart`). `dateEnd` must not be before `dateStart`.

Elevation.name: elevation
Elevation.description:
Elevation of the location above sea level in meters. Used to
refine astronomical calculations.

When not provided, the elevation of the nearest known city to the
resolved coordinates is used automatically; it falls back to `0`
only when no elevation data is available for that location.
Maximum allowed value is **10,000 meters**; only this upper bound
is enforced (HTTP 400 if exceeded). Negative values are accepted
without an error.

TimeZone.name: time_zone
TimeZone.description:
IANA timezone identifier used to convert all astronomical event
timestamps into the specified timezone.

When provided, all event times (sunrise, sunset, moonrise, moonset,
twilight phases, solar noon, etc.) are returned as full date-time
values (`yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`) instead of time-only values (`HH:mm`),
and a `time_zone` field is included in the `astronomy` object.

The geographic location used for astronomical calculations remains
unchanged. Only the timestamp representation is converted.

Example: `Europe/London`, `America/New_York`, `Asia/Karachi`.

Lang.name: lang
Lang.description:
Language code for translated location names in the `location` object.
Only applies when the lookup is performed via an IP address.

Defaults to `en`. Non-English responses require a paid plan.
Requesting a non-English `lang` value on a Free/Developer plan
returns HTTP 401 (see the `freePlanLang` example under the 401
response) rather than silently falling back to English. Unsupported
`lang` values return HTTP 400 on `/v3/astronomy`. On
`/v3/astronomy/timeSeries` the value is not validated: on paid plans an
unsupported value returns English names, and on a Free plan any value
other than `en` returns HTTP 401.

Output.name: output
Output.description:
Desired response format. Defaults to `json` if not specified. You can also
control the format using the `Accept` header (`application/json`,
`application/xml`, or `text/xml`). For successful responses and authentication
errors, the `Accept` header takes precedence if both are provided: `output` is
used only when the `Accept` header is absent or set to `*/*`, and an `Accept`
value other than `application/xml` or `text/xml` (for example a browser's
default) returns JSON even with `output=xml`. Values are matched exactly (use
lowercase `xml`).

If `output` is unknown or unsupported, it is ignored and the response defaults
to JSON (`application/json`) with HTTP 200.

NotFound.description:
Not Found. Returned for one of the following reasons:
  - If the IPv4 or IPv6 address is passed as a path variable instead
    of a URL parameter (`ip=`).
  - If the location address provided to the `location` parameter is
    invalid. A city-level or state-level address must be provided.
  - If the wrong endpoint is called that does not exist in the API.

value.message: We couldn't find the location (InvalidCity, XX). Try a city or state level location address only.
No endpoint GET /v3/astronomy-invalid.

NotFoundTimeSeries.description:
Not Found. Returned for one of the following reasons:

    of a URL parameter (`ip=`).
  - If the location address provided to the `location` parameter is
    invalid. A city-level or state-level address must be provided.
  - If the wrong endpoint is called that does not exist in the API.

MethodNotAllowed.description:
Method Not Allowed. Only the **GET** method is supported for
Astronomy API endpoints. Calling an endpoint with an HTTP method it doesn't support
(for example `PUT` or `DELETE`) results in HTTP 405.

Locked.description:
Locked. The provided IP address belongs to a bogon IP range or a
private network and cannot be looked up.

TooManyRequests.description:
Too Many Requests. Returned for one of the following reasons:
  - The API credit allowance has been reached for a free subscription.
  - The API credit allowance has been reached for an active trial
    subscription (capped at 100,000 API credits).
  - The API credit allowance has been reached for a paid subscription with
    surcharge usage disabled.
  - The API credit allowance has been reached for a paid subscription with
    status `past due` or `deleted`.
  - The surcharge (overage) credit limit has been reached for the subscribed
    plan.

ClientClosedRequest.description:
The client closed the connection before the server finished processing
the request (logged by the edge proxy; the client receives no response).
This usually happens when the client sets a very short request or
connection timeout. Increase the timeout on the client side.

InternalServerError.description:
Internal Server Error. The server encountered an unexpected condition
that prevented it from fulfilling the request. If the issue persists,
contact support@ipgeolocation.io.

example.message: Something went wrong while processing your request. Please try again or contact technical support at support@ipgeolocation.io

BadGateway.description:
Bad Gateway. Returned by the edge proxy in front of the API, not by the API
application, when it gets an invalid response from the API server. The
response body is set by the proxy. This is usually temporary; retry the
request.

ServiceUnavailable.description:
Service Unavailable. Returned when the API cannot verify your API key (or request
origin) because of a temporary internal error, for example when the billing service
is unreachable and the key has not been verified recently. Keys that were verified
recently keep working. Retry later; if it persists, contact support@ipgeolocation.io.

Also returned when a `location` value cannot be geocoded because the geocoding
service is temporarily unavailable. Retry, or use coordinates.

We couldn't look up the location (London, UK) right now. Please try again shortly, or use the 'lat' and 'long' parameters instead.

GatewayTimeout.description:
Gateway Timeout. Returned by the edge proxy in front of the API, not by the
API application, when the API server does not respond in time. The response
body is set by the proxy. Retry the request.

HttpVersionNotSupported.description:
HTTP Version Not Supported. Returned by the edge proxy in front of the API,
not by the API application, when the request uses an HTTP protocol version
it does not support. The response body is set by the proxy.

PaymentRequired.description:
Payment Required. Returned for a paid (non-Free) subscription whose active-until
date has passed: one day after the active-until date for active or trialing
subscriptions, and from the active-until date for past-due or deleted
subscriptions. It is checked before any usage quota. Paused subscriptions and
expired trials get HTTP 401 instead, and Free plan keys never get 402. Renew or
upgrade the plan to continue using IPGeolocation API.

ErrorResponse.description:
Returned for any non-200 response. Contains only a human-readable
`message`. Message text can vary by status and condition; examples
in this spec are representative, not exhaustive, and should not be
treated as stable machine codes.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of what went wrong.
message.example: '999.999.999.999' is not an IP string literal.

AstronomyLookupResponse.description:
Response returned by the single-date Astronomy Lookup API.

Contains a `location` object with geolocation details for the
resolved location, and an `astronomy` object with astronomical
event times and positional data for the requested date.

The `location` object structure varies based on the lookup method:
- Coordinate or location-based lookups return basic geographic fields.
- IP-based lookups return extended geolocation fields including
  continent, country codes, district, and zipcode.

ip.description:
The IP address used for the astronomy lookup. Returned only when
the lookup is performed using the `ip` parameter or when the API
resolves the caller's IP automatically (no parameters provided).

AstronomyTimeSeriesResponse.description:
Response returned by the Astronomy Time Series API.

Contains a `location` object and an `astronomy` array where each
element represents astronomical data for a single day within the
requested date range.

Note that real-time positional data (sun/moon altitude, azimuth,
distance, parallactic angle, illumination) is not included in time
series responses.

ip.description:
The IP address used for the astronomy lookup. Returned only when
the lookup is performed using the `ip` parameter or when the API
resolves the caller's IP automatically.

astronomy.description:
Array of daily astronomical records covering the requested date
range. Each entry contains event times for one calendar day.

Location.description:
Geolocation information associated with the resolved location.

For coordinate-based or location-string lookups, only basic geographic
fields are returned (latitude, longitude, country, state, city, locality,
elevation).

For IP-based lookups, extended fields are also returned including
continent codes, country codes, district, zipcode, and other metadata.

location_string.description:
The location string provided in the request. Only present when the
`location` query parameter was used.

continent_code.description: Two-letter continent code. Returned for IP-based lookups only.

continent_name.description: Full name of the continent. Returned for IP-based lookups only.

country_code2.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Returned for IP-based lookups only.

country_code3.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code. Returned for IP-based lookups only.

country_name_official.description: Official name of the country. Returned for IP-based lookups only.

is_eu.description:
Indicates whether the country is a member of the European Union.
Returned for IP-based lookups only.

state_code.description: Standardized state or region code. Returned for IP-based lookups only.

district.description:
District or administrative subdivision. Returned for IP-based
lookups only.

locality.description: Smaller locality or neighborhood within the city.

zipcode.description:
ZIP or postal code of the location. Returned for IP-based
lookups only.

latitude.description: Latitude coordinate of the resolved location.

longitude.description: Longitude coordinate of the resolved location.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters of the nearest known city, as a string. Empty string when not available. It does not echo the `elevation` request parameter.

TwilightPhase.description:
Twilight phase times for either the morning (pre-sunrise) or evening
(post-sunset) period.

Includes astronomical, nautical, and civil twilight windows, as well
as blue hour and golden hour windows commonly used in photography.

All times are in `HH:mm` format by default. When the `time_zone`
parameter is provided, times are returned as full date-time values
in `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm` format.

astronomical_twilight_begin.description:
Start of astronomical twilight. In the morning, this is the end of
night (same as `night_end`). In the evening, it is the end of nautical
twilight; night starts at the evening `astronomical_twilight_end`
(same as `night_begin`).

nautical_twilight_begin.description: Start of nautical twilight, when the horizon first becomes visible.

civil_twilight_begin.description:
Start of civil twilight, when there is enough light for outdoor
activities without artificial lighting.

blue_hour_begin.description:
Start of the blue hour, a period of soft diffused light with a
blue color tone.

golden_hour_begin.description:
Start of the golden hour, a period of warm low-angle light
favored by photographers.

AstronomyData.description:
Astronomical data for the resolved location and requested date.

Includes event times for sunrise, sunset, moonrise, moonset,
twilight phases, golden hour, blue hour, solar noon, and
astronomical midnight, as well as real-time positional data
for the Sun and Moon at the current time of day.

All timestamp fields (except `current_time` and `day_length`) are
in `HH:mm` format by default. When the `time_zone` parameter is
provided, they are returned as full date-time values in
`yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm` format.

time_zone.description:
The IANA timezone identifier used for timestamp conversion.
This field appears only when the `time_zone` query parameter
was provided in the request.

date.description: The date for which astronomical data is returned, in `yyyy-MM-dd` format.

current_time.description:
Current time in `HH:mm:ss.SSS` format, in the location's time zone, or in
`time_zone` when that parameter is given. Positional values (altitude,
azimuth, distance) are calculated for this time. Without `date`, the
current date is also taken in that time zone.

mid_night.description: Astronomical midnight (nadir) for the given date, in `HH:mm` format.

night_end.description:
End of night / start of astronomical twilight in the morning,
in `HH:mm` format.

sunrise.description:
Time at which the sun rises at the resolved location, in `HH:mm`
format. Returns `"-:-"` if the sun does not rise on this date
(polar day or polar night).

sunset.description:
Time at which the sun sets at the resolved location, in `HH:mm`
format. Returns `"-:-"` if the sun does not set on this date
(polar day or polar night).

night_begin.description:
Start of night / end of astronomical twilight in the evening,
in `HH:mm` format.

sun_status.description:
Represents the current state of the sun relative to the horizon:

- `"-"` — Normal day with both sunrise and sunset occurring.
- `"Always above the twilight angle"` — The sun does not set
  (perpetual daylight, e.g. polar summer).
- `"Always below the twilight angle"` — The sun does not rise
  within the current 24-hour period (e.g. polar night).

solar_noon.description:
The time when the sun is at its highest point in the sky,
in `HH:mm` format.

day_length.description:
Total length of daylight for the date, from sunrise to sunset,
in `HH:mm` format. Returns `"-:-"` if sunrise or sunset does
not occur on this date (polar day or polar night).

sun_altitude.description:
The sun's altitude angle above the horizon at `current_time`,
measured in degrees. Negative values indicate the sun is below
the horizon.

sun_distance.description: Distance from Earth to the sun at `current_time`, in kilometers.

sun_azimuth.description:
The azimuth angle of the sun at `current_time`, indicating its
compass direction in degrees (0° = North, 90° = East, etc.).

moon_phase.description:
The current phase of the moon, indicating its position in the
lunar cycle.

moonrise.description:
Time at which the moon rises at the resolved location, in `HH:mm`
format. Returns `"-:-"` if the moon does not rise on this date.

moonset.description:
Time at which the moon sets at the resolved location, in `HH:mm`
format. Returns `"-:-"` if the moon does not set on this date.

moon_status.description:
Represents the current state of the moon relative to the horizon:

- `"-"` — Normal day with both moonrise and moonset occurring.
- `"Always above the horizon"` — The moon does not set within
  the current 24-hour period.
- `"Always below the horizon"` — The moon does not rise within
  the current 24-hour period.

moon_altitude.description:
The moon's altitude angle above the horizon at `current_time`,
measured in degrees. Negative values indicate the moon is below
the horizon.

moon_distance.description: Distance from Earth to the moon at `current_time`, in kilometers.

moon_azimuth.description:
The azimuth angle of the moon at `current_time`, indicating its
compass direction in degrees.

moon_parallactic_angle.description:
The angle between the celestial pole and the moon's position
relative to the observer's location, measured in degrees.

moon_illumination_percentage.description:
The percentage of the moon's surface illuminated by sunlight
as viewed from Earth. Returned as a string with two decimal
places. Negative values indicate a waning phase.

moon_angle.description:
The moon-sun ecliptic elongation angle, normalized to the
0–360° range. This is the phase angle used to derive
`moon_phase` and `moon_illumination_percentage`; it is not
the moon's angular diameter.

AstronomyTimeSeriesEntry.description:
Astronomical data for a single calendar day within the time series
response.

Contains event times for sunrise, sunset, moonrise, moonset,
twilight phases, solar noon, and day length.

Note: Real-time positional data (sun/moon altitude, azimuth,
distance, parallactic angle, illumination percentage, and moon
angle) is not included in time series entries.

time_zone.description:
The IANA timezone identifier used for timestamp conversion.
This field appears only when the `time_zone` query parameter
was provided in the request.

date.description: The calendar date for this entry, in `yyyy-MM-dd` format.

mid_night.description: Astronomical midnight (nadir) for the given date.

night_end.description: End of night / start of astronomical twilight in the morning.

sunrise.description:
Time at which the sun rises, in `HH:mm` format. Returns `"-:-"`
if the sun does not rise on this date.

sunset.description:
Time at which the sun sets, in `HH:mm` format. Returns `"-:-"`
if the sun does not set on this date.

night_begin.description: Start of night / end of astronomical twilight in the evening.

sun_status.description:
Current state of the sun relative to the horizon. See
`AstronomyData.sun_status` for possible values.

solar_noon.description: Time when the sun is at its highest point in the sky.

day_length.description:
Total daylight duration from sunrise to sunset, in `HH:mm`
format. Returns `"-:-"` if sunrise or sunset does not occur
on this date (polar day or polar night).

moon_phase.description: The phase of the moon on this date.

moonrise.description:
Time at which the moon rises, in `HH:mm` format. Returns `"-:-"`
if the moon does not rise on this date.

moonset.description:
Time at which the moon sets, in `HH:mm` format. Returns `"-:-"`
if the moon does not set on this date.

moon_status.description:
Current state of the moon relative to the horizon. See
`AstronomyData.moon_status` for possible values.

ApiKeyAuth.name: apiKey
ApiKeyAuth.description:
API key passed as the `apiKey` query parameter. Get yours from the
[IPGeolocation dashboard](https://app.ipgeolocation.io/). For
client-side usage on paid plans, consider using Request Origin (CORS)
authentication to avoid exposing your key.
